issuer: the Especialidad de Seguridad de Tránsito de la Policía Nacional
note: Read 2026-10-31. Law 431 (Ley para el Régimen de Circulación Vehicular e Infracciones de Tránsito), in the text with its reforms published in La Gaceta No. 96 of 27 May 2014, as the National Police host it: art. 140, the licence is issued by the Especialidad de Seguridad de Tránsito of the National Police and is valid throughout the country for five years; the ordinary licence is issued to those who reach the age of majority or more applying for the first time (a minor's licence, from sixteen with a parent's or guardian's authorisation, expires at majority). The age of majority is the Family Code's (Law 870, La Gaceta No. 190 of 8 October 2014, art. 301): eighteen years completed, for all purposes; the Code was read in the copy ecoi.net hosts, not on a Nicaraguan government site. The consolidated text of Law 431 published in La Gaceta No. 09 of 18 January 2024 (Digesto Jurídico, as of 28 February 2023) was read in the copy leybook.com hosts (an aggregator, not cited) and keeps art. 140's five years and the ordinary licence at majority word for word. The fee is null: the 2014 text's art. 145 charges C$200 for a licence, but its fee table is an image in the 2024 text and La Prensa reported on 27 March 2026 a rise in the police's licence fees, so the 2014 amount isn't the one in force.

La licencia de conducir es expedida por la Especialidad de Seguridad ... de Tránsito de la Policía Nacional
